assumptions: The plan feeds four people to safely cover the stated requirement of three to four people.
Common cupboard basics such as cooking oil, salt, pepper, stock cubes, dried herbs and mayonnaise are included only where a top-up may be needed.
Pack sizes are practical UK supermarket sizes and may be adjusted to the nearest available equivalent.
Lunch portions can be reduced for young children; unused cooked food should be chilled promptly and used within two days or frozen.
The week begins on the next Monday after the spreadsheet was reviewed.

breakfast.meal: Ready Brek with soy milk, banana and blueberries
breakfast.notes: Uses the most delicate berries first. Slice only the bananas needed so the rest keep longer.

lunch.notes: Open the ham and grapes early in the week. Freeze half the bread on shopping day and defrost later slices as needed.

dinner.notes: Fresh salmon and broccoli are scheduled first because they are among the most perishable ingredients. Roast extra potato wedges for Tuesday lunch.

breakfast.meal: Toast with peanut butter or jam
breakfast.notes: Use the opened bread; toast works well even if slices have been frozen.

lunch.meal: Mackerel and vegetable rice with leftover potato wedges
lunch.notes: Tinned mackerel and packet rice make a quick lunch; yesterday's wedges avoid waste and can be reheated until piping hot.

dinner.notes: Uses fresh lettuce and peppers while crisp. Cook one extra chicken portion for Wednesday lunch and keep lettuce dry in a sealed container.

breakfast.notes: Uses soy milk and eggs already required for the week. Very ripe banana can be mashed into the batter.

lunch.notes: Uses the reserved cooked fajita chicken and any remaining lettuce or wraps. Keep cooked chicken chilled and use within two days.

dinner.meal: Spaghetti Bolognese with carrot, celery and onion
dinner.notes: Carrot, celery and onion form the requested base. Make eight portions: serve four and refrigerate or freeze four for Saturday to save cooking and prevent half-used vegetable packs.

breakfast.notes: A low-preparation breakfast; keep cereal airtight and use the opened soy milk first.

lunch.meal: Leek, potato and carrot soup with seeded bread
lunch.notes: Uses remaining potatoes and carrots plus part of the leek pack. Make extra soup and freeze portions if not needed on Sunday.

dinner.meal: Roast chicken dinner with roast potatoes, carrots and peas
dinner.notes: Roast a whole chicken and reserve about 350 g cooked meat for Friday's stir-fry. Freeze the carcass for stock or simmer it with vegetable trimmings.

breakfast.meal: Ready Brek with soy milk and apple
breakfast.notes: Apples keep well and balance the remaining fresh fruit through the second half of the week.

lunch.notes: A store-cupboard lunch that uses the second loaf after defrosting and requires no extra perishable filling.

dinner.meal: Chicken stir-fry with noodles, peppers, onion, sweetcorn and peas
dinner.notes: Uses the reserved roast chicken plus remaining peppers and onion. Frozen sweetcorn and peas mean no half-used fresh packs.

breakfast.notes: Bacon is placed later because an unopened pack keeps well; freeze any unused rashers in separated portions.

lunch.meal: Leek, potato and carrot soup with bread
lunch.notes: Uses Thursday's extra soup. If it was frozen, thaw safely and reheat until piping hot.

dinner.notes: Uses the extra batch made Wednesday. If refrigerated, eat within two days; otherwise freeze Wednesday and defrost in the fridge before reheating.

breakfast.notes: Finishes the week's fruit and uses the same long-life pancake staples without opening another cereal box.

lunch.meal: Jacket potatoes with tuna, cheese and beans
lunch.notes: A flexible lunch for using remaining potatoes, cheese and opened beans. Bake one potato per adult and smaller ones for children.

waste_reduction_summary: Cook salmon, broccoli, berries, grapes, lettuce and opened ham early; rely on frozen and cupboard ingredients near the weekend.
Cook double Bolognese on Wednesday and reuse it Saturday, freezing Wednesday if it cannot be eaten within two days.
Roast one whole chicken Thursday, reserve cooked meat for Friday stir-fry, and freeze the carcass for stock.
Use the same potato, carrot, onion and pepper packs across multiple meals so packs are substantially consumed in one week.
Freeze one bread loaf immediately and defrost individual slices; freeze surplus wraps, bacon and overripe bananas before quality declines.
Check existing Essentials and freezer stock before shopping because the source sheet records preferred staples, not current inventory.
Label chilled leftovers with the cooked date, cool promptly, and freeze anything that will not be eaten within two days.
